category_title: Students who engage in disruptive behavior to avoid difficult academic tasks
minimal_context: David is presented with a reading assignment during his English Language Arts class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: David, it is time for ELA. Please read this passage and complete the assignment at your desk.

STUDENT: (Stares at the paper) I'm not reading this. It's too long.

TUTOR: You need to do your work. Just get started.

STUDENT: (Pushes the assignment off the desk) No! I'm not doing it.

TUTOR: David, pick up your paper right now or I will have to send you to the office.

STUDENT: I don't give a s***! Send me to the office, I'm not doing this f***ing reading!

options.A: Invite the student to participate in choral reading of a shared text with classmates during regular classroom instruction.
options.B: Preview key vocabulary and concepts covered in the lesson (e.g., prefixes, suffixes, base words) to familiarize the student with the next day's reading assignment.
options.C: Ask follow-up questions about the reading assignment to model conversational skills for the student during regular classroom instruction.
options.D: Adjust the ratio of lower-level to higher-level questions based on the student's reading level, keeping the percentage of lower-level questions highest for the student.
